<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:closed-imm}
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is a closed immersion.
\item For every affine open $U = \operatorname{Spec} R \subseteq X$ there is an ideal
      $I \subseteq R$ with $i^{-1}(U) \cong \operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ as schemes over $U$.
\item There is an affine open cover $X = \bigcup_{j \in J} U_j$, with
      $U_j = \operatorname{Spec} R_j$, and for each $j$ an ideal $I_j \subseteq R_j$ with
      $i^{-1}(U_j) \cong \operatorname{Spec}(R_j / I_j)$ as schemes over $U_j$.
\item $i$ induces a homeomorphism of $Z$ onto a closed subset of $X$ and
      $i^{\sharp} : \mathcal{O}_X \to i_* \mathcal{O}_Z$ is surjective.
\item $i$ induces a homeomorphism of $Z$ onto a closed subset of $X$,
      $i^{\sharp}$ is surjective, and $\ker(i^{\sharp}) \subseteq \mathcal{O}_X$ is a
      quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.
\item $i$ induces a homeomorphism of $Z$ onto a closed subset of $X$,
      $i^{\sharp}$ is surjective, and $\ker(i^{\sharp}) \subseteq \mathcal{O}_X$ is a
      sheaf of ideals which is locally generated by sections.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:preclos}
A \emph{presented centre} on $X$ consists of:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a type $\iota$ of indices;
\item for each $i \in \iota$, a scheme $Z_i$ together with a morphism
      $Z_i \to X$;
\item an affine open cover $\mathcal{U} = \bigl( u_\gamma : \operatorname{Spec} A_\gamma \to X
      \bigr)_{\gamma \in J}$ of $X$ by open immersions;
\item for each $i$ and $\gamma$, an ideal $I_{i\gamma} \subseteq A_\gamma$;
\item for each $i$ and $\gamma$, an isomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec} A_\gamma$-schemes
\[
  \operatorname{Spec}\bigl(A_\gamma / I_{i\gamma}\bigr)
  \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;
  Z_i \times_X \operatorname{Spec} A_\gamma .
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:rel}
Two presented centres $Z, Z'$ are \emph{equivalent} if there is a bijection
$\sigma : \iota \to \iota'$ of index types and isomorphisms
$Z_i \cong Z'_{\sigma(i)}$ over $X$ for every $i$. A \emph{centre} on $X$ is an
equivalence class. We write $\operatorname{Clos}(X)$ for the set of centres.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def:cartier}
A presented centre $Z$ is \emph{Cartier} if for every $i \in \iota$ and every
$\gamma \in J$ the ideal $I_{i\gamma} \subseteq A_\gamma$ is principal and
generated by a non-zero-divisor. A centre $\mathcal{Z} \in \operatorname{Clos}(X)$ is Cartier if
\emph{some} presentation of $\mathcal{Z}$ is Cartier.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main-pre}
Let $Z$ be a presented centre on $X$ with finite index type. Let $T$ be a
scheme over $X$, with structure morphism $f : T \to X$. If the pulled back
presented centre $f^*Z$ is Cartier, then there is exactly one morphism
\[
  \varphi : T \longrightarrow \operatorname{Bl}_Z X
\]
over $X$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
Let $\mathcal{Z} \in \operatorname{Clos}(X)$ be a centre with finite index type and let $T$ be a
scheme over $X$ with structure morphism $f$. If $f^*\mathcal{Z}$ is Cartier, then there
is exactly one morphism $T \to \operatorname{Bl}_\mathcal{Z} X$ over $X$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:blglob-cartier}
The centre pulled back to $\operatorname{Bl}_Z X$ is Cartier.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:terminal}
$\operatorname{Bl}_\mathcal{Z} X$ is a terminal object of $\mathcal{C}_\mathcal{Z}$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:multicenter}
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. A \emph{multicenter} on $A$ is a triple
$F = (\Lambda, (I_j)_{j \in \Lambda}, (a_j)_{j \in \Lambda})$ where $\Lambda$
is a type, each $I_j$ is an ideal of $A$ and each $a_j$ is an element of $A$.
The \emph{large ideal} at $j$ is
\[
  \mathcal{L}_j \;:=\; I_j + (a_j).
\]
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:dilatation}
The \emph{dilatation} of $A$ along $F$ is
\[
  A[F] \;:=\;
  \Bigl\{\, \tfrac{m}{a^\nu} \;:\; \nu \in \Lambda^{(\mathbb{N})},\;
     m \in \mathcal{L}^\nu \,\Bigr\} \Big/ \sim,
\]
where
\[
  \frac{m}{a^{\nu}} \sim \frac{n}{a^{\mu}}
  \iff
  \exists\, \beta \in \Lambda^{(\mathbb{N})} : \quad
  m \, a^{\beta + \mu} \;=\; n \, a^{\beta + \nu} .
\]
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:dil-nzd}
For every $\nu$, the image of $a^\nu$ in $A[F]$ is a non-zero-divisor.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:dil-gen}
For every $\nu$, inside $A[F]$ one has
\[
  \bigl( a^{\nu} \bigr) \;=\; \mathcal{L}^{\nu} \cdot A[F].
\]
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:dil-univ}
Let $B$ be an $A$-algebra such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the image of $a_j$ in $B$ is a non-zero-divisor for every $j$, and
\item $(a_j) = \mathcal{L}_j B$ inside $B$, for every $j$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there is exactly one morphism of $A$-algebras $A[F] \to B$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:dil-trivial}
If every $a_j$ is already a non-zero-divisor in $A$ and $\mathcal{L}_j = (a_j)$, then
$A \to A[F]$ is an isomorphism.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:dil-eq}
If $F = F'$ as multicenters then $A[F] = A[F']$, canonically and uniquely.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:dil-funct}
There is a unique morphism of $A$-algebras $A[F] \to B[F_B]$ compatible with
$A \to B$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:pres}
A \emph{presentation} of $L$ is a multicenter $F$ on $A$ with finite index type
$\Lambda$, together with maps $\Psi : \Lambda \to \iota$ and
$s : \iota \to \Lambda$ such that
\[
  \Psi \circ s = \mathrm{id}_\iota,
  \qquad
  \mathcal{L}_j = L_{\Psi(j)} \quad \text{for all } j \in \Lambda .
\]
We write $\mathcal{M}(L)$ for the collection of presentations.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:dil-is-potion}
There is a canonical isomorphism of $A$-algebras
\[
  A[F] \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\; \operatorname{Pot}(S_F).
\]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:blm}
$\operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L) := \operatorname{Proj}$ of $\operatorname{Rees}(L)$ taken over the family
$\{ S_F : F \in \mathcal{M}(L)\}$, that is, the scheme obtained by gluing the affine
charts $\operatorname{Spec} \operatorname{Pot}(S_F) \cong \operatorname{Spec} A[F]$, $F \in \mathcal{M}(L)$, along the standard
$\operatorname{Proj}$ gluing data. It carries a structure morphism $\operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L) \to \operatorname{Spec} A$
induced by $A \cong \operatorname{Rees}(L)_0$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:blm-cartier}
The centre $L$ pulled back to $\operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L)$ is Cartier.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:aff-uniq}
Let $T$ be a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec} A$ on which $L$ becomes Cartier. Then any two
morphisms $T \to \operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L)$ over $\operatorname{Spec} A$ are equal.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:aff-exist}
Let $T$ be a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec} A$ on which $L$ becomes Cartier. Then there is
a morphism $T \to \operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L)$ over $\operatorname{Spec} A$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:aff-main}
$\operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L)$ is terminal among $\operatorname{Spec} A$-schemes on which $L$ becomes Cartier.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:bc}
Let $A \to B$ be a ring map with $\operatorname{Spec} B \to \operatorname{Spec} A$ an open immersion, and
let $L' := (L_i B)_i$. Then there is exactly one isomorphism
\[
  \operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L) \times_{\operatorname{Spec} A} \operatorname{Spec} B \;\cong\; \operatorname{Bl}^{\mathrm{aff}}(L')
\]
over $\operatorname{Spec} B$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:swap}
There is exactly one isomorphism
\[
  t_{\gamma\delta} : V_{\gamma\delta} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } V_{\delta\gamma}
\]
over $U_{\gamma\delta}$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:glob-cartier}
The centre pulled back to $\operatorname{Bl}_Z X$ is Cartier.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:rel}
If $Z'$ and $Z''$ are equivalent presented centres, then there is exactly one
isomorphism $\operatorname{Bl}_{Z'} X \cong \operatorname{Bl}_{Z''} X$ over $X$.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
